x.ASV: Praise ye Jehovah. I will give thanks unto Jehovah with my whole heart, In the council of the upright, and in the congregation.
x.Darby: Hallelujah! I will celebrate Jehovah with [my] whole heart, in the council of the upright, and in the assembly.
x.KJV: Praise ye the Lord. I will praise the Lord with my whole heart, in the assembly of the upright, and in the congregation.
x.YLT: Praise ye Jah! I thank Jehovah with the whole heart, In the secret meeting of the upright, And of the company.

nt: The words **Hallelu Yah** are Hebrew words, containing a plural command to praise Yahweh. You will need to decide if you will use these words in their Hebrew form or if you will instead translate the meaning into your language. Either approach has broad support. If you use the Hebrew words, you could spell them the way that they sound in your language and then put the translation in a footnote. Alternate translation: [Halleluia] or [Praise Yah]
**Yah** is a shortened form of the name “Yahweh,” the God of Israel. You could use the full name if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [Yahweh]

Here the psalmist is speaking of the place where his emotions and will reside as his **heart**. You may have a comparable expression in your language, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [with my whole heart] or [with all that I am]

The phrase **upright and congregation** expresses a single idea. The word **upright** tells more about **congregation**. If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this meaning in a different way. Alternate translation: [the congregation of upright people]

The psalmist is using the adjective **upright** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [the upright people]

x.ASV: The works of Jehovah are great, Sought out of all them that have pleasure therein.
x.Darby: Great are the works of Jehovah; sought out of all that delight in them.
x.KJV: The works of the Lord are great, sought out of all them that have pleasure therein.
x.YLT: Great are the works of Jehovah, Sought out by all desiring them.

nt: The expression **searched by everyone desirous of them** contains a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [everyone desirous of them searches them]

The psalmist is using the adjective **desirous** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [searched by everyone who desires them]
The pronoun **them** refers to the works of Yahweh. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [they are searched by everyone desirous of his works]
This could mean: (1) people examine and study Yahweh’s works. Alternate translation: [studied] or (2) people are looking for Yahweh to do his works. Alternate translation: [eagerly awaited]

x.ASV: His work is honor and majesty; And his righteousness endureth for ever.
x.Darby: His work is majesty and splendour, and his righteousness abideth for ever.
x.KJV: His work is honourable and glorious: and his righteousness endureth for ever.
x.YLT: Honourable and majestic is His work, And His righteousness is standing for ever.

nt: If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **splendor** and **majesty**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [His work is splendid and majestic]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **righteousness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and he is righteous forever]

Here the psalmist is speaking of God’s righteousness as if it were a structure that **stands forever**. He means that God’s righteousness is permanent and will never change or fail. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and his righteousness endures forever]

x.ASV: He hath made his wonderful works to be remembered: Jehovah is gracious and merciful.
x.Darby: He hath made his wonders to be remembered: Jehovah is gracious and merciful.
x.KJV: He hath made his wonderful works to be remembered: the Lord is gracious and full of compassion.
x.YLT: A memorial He hath made of His wonders, Gracious and merciful is Jehovah.

nt: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **remembrance**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [He makes sure that people will always remember the wonderful things that he does]

x.ASV: He hath given food unto them that fear him: He will ever be mindful of his covenant.
x.Darby: He hath given meat unto them that fear him; he is ever mindful of his covenant.
x.KJV: He hath given meat unto them that fear him: he will ever be mindful of his covenant.
x.YLT: Prey He hath given to those fearing Him, He remembereth to the age His covenant.

nt: The psalmist is using the adjective **fearing** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [to the people who fear him]
This means that Yahweh will always act according to his covenant. See how you translated this in [Psalm 105:8](../105/008.md). Alternate translation: [He will honor his covenant forever]

x.ASV: He hath showed his people the power of his works, In giving them the heritage of the nations.
x.Darby: He hath shewn his people the power of his works, to give them the heritage of the nations.
x.KJV: He hath shewed his people the power of his works, that he may give them the heritage of the heathen.
x.YLT: The power of His works He hath declared to His people, To give to them the inheritance of nations.

nt: The psalmist is using the possessive form to describe **works** that are characterized by **power**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [his powerful works]

The implication is that Yahweh showed his power by means of giving his people the lands that had belonged to other nations as their inheritance. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [by giving to them]

The implication is that this refers to the land that belonged to other nations. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [land that belonged to other nations]

x.ASV: The works of his hands are truth and justice; All his precepts are sure.
x.Darby: The works of his hands are truth and judgment; all his precepts are faithful:
x.KJV: The works of his hands are verity and judgment; all his commandments are sure.
x.YLT: The works of His hands are true and just, Stedfast are all His appointments.

nt: Here the psalmist is speaking of the things that God does as if they were **the works of his hands**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [All the things that he does]
If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **truth** and **justice**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [are true and just]

The psalmist assumes that readers will know that **precepts** refers to God’s commands and instructions. You could say that explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [We can rely on all of his instructions]

x.ASV: They are established for ever and ever; They are done in truth and uprightness.
x.Darby: Maintained for ever and ever, done in truth and uprightness.
x.KJV: They stand fast for ever and ever, and are done in truth and uprightness.
x.YLT: They are sustained for ever to the age. They are made in truth and uprightness.

nt: The expression **They are established** contains a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is Yahweh. Alternate translation: [He established them to last forever]

The terms **forever** and **for eternity** mean similar things. The psalmist is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [for all eternity]

If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. This could mean: (1) Yahweh has given his instructions in a faithful and proper manner. Alternate translation: [made faithfully and uprightly] or (2) his people are to observe Yahweh’s instructions in a faithful and proper manner. Alternate translation: [for his people to observe faithfully and properly]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **faithfulness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [done faithfully]

The psalmist is using the adjective **upright** as a noun to mean upright things or upright instructions. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [and they are instructions that are upright]

x.ASV: He hath sent redemption unto his people; He hath commanded his covenant for ever: Holy and reverend is his name.
x.Darby: He sent deliverance unto his people; he hath commanded his covenant for ever: holy and terrible is his name.
x.KJV: He sent redemption unto his people: he hath commanded his covenant for ever: holy and reverend is his name.
x.YLT: Redemption He hath sent to His people, He hath appointed to the age His covenant, Holy and fearful is His name.

nt: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **redemption**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [He has redeemed his people]

The psalmist is using the term **name** to represent who Yahweh is or to refer to Yahweh’s reputation. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Yahweh is holy and awesome]

x.ASV: The fear of Jehovah is the beginning of wisdom; A good understanding have all they that do his commandments: His praise endureth for ever.
x.Darby: The fear of Jehovah is the beginning of wisdom; a good understanding have all they that do [his precepts]: his praise abideth for ever.
x.KJV: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments: his praise endureth for ever.
x.YLT: The beginning of wisdom is fear of Jehovah, Good understanding have all doing them, His praise is standing for ever!

nt: The psalmist is using this possessive form to mean a deep reverence for Yahweh. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. See how you translated this in [Psalm 19:9](../019/009.md). Alternate translation: [Revering Yahweh]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **wisdom**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [is how a person begins to become wise]

The psalmist is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [all those doing them will gain a good understanding of how to live well]
The pronoun **them** refers to Yahweh’s precepts, mentioned in verse 7. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [to all those doing his precepts]

Here the psalmist is speaking of **praise** as if it were something that could **stand** in the sense of remaining upright and stable. He means that God will be praised forever. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [His praise endures forever] or [He is to be praised forever]
